names_for.catalogue_side: AI 허브 개방 데이터 (AI-Hub open data), alongside 기관 제공 데이터 (institution-provided data) and 독자 AI모델 데이터 (sovereign AI model data)
names_for.custom_side: none on AI-Hub itself; it links out to private 'AI데이터 거래소' (AI data exchanges)

operator_role.note: NIA co-holds rights in, and sets the terms for, the data it commissioned; for institution-provided data AI-Hub only presents the listing and the provider's own terms apply.

economics_model.note: Government-funded; no charge to users found anywhere on the site.

who_pays_fee.note: No fee is charged to users or providers.

supply_models.note: own_collection = datasets NIA commissions from vendor consortia under government programmes, with rights co-held by NIA and the builders; third_party_providers = institution-provided data, sovereign-model team data, company and university data.

custody_model.note: Open data is downloaded to the user's machine; safe-zone data stays on NIA servers; institution-provided data and linked exchanges are presented as listings or links only.

transaction_mode.note: Application with stated purpose; auto-approved for most open data, reviewed for other data and the safe zone.

public_prices.note: Data is distributed free of charge.

licence_model.note: One standard AI-Hub usage policy for NIA data; institution-provided and some hosted datasets (KETI, competition data) carry their own terms.

public_listing.note: Dataset pages with schema, statistics and builder contacts load without login; the data and even the sample button require login.

buyer_vetting.note: Identity-verified Korean nationals get auto-approval for most open data; review data and the safe zone are checked per application (IRB for medical data).

sample_mechanics.note: A processed 'sample (light) data' file is offered per dataset; in the page markup the button calls a login prompt for anonymous visitors.

versioning.note: Dataset pages show a version change history (c065, c056) but nothing says whether earlier versions stay available.

human_subject_consent_docs.note: Listings assert that portrait rights were resolved and data de-identified; no consent or release documents are offered to users.

contributor_pay_model.note: Data is given away, not sold, so no sale proceeds reach individual capturers or labellers; how builders pay crowd workers is not published.

catalogue_plus_custom.note: No build-to-order service for users was found; bespoke collection sits with the private exchanges AI-Hub links to.

erasure_after_sale.note: Users must delete a dataset if personal information is found, and NIA may demand return or destruction.

quality_evidence.note: Listings show validation-model scores produced by the building consortium (c073); whether NIA or a third party checks them was not found.

Q1.answer: Users are Korean researchers, companies and public bodies who download whole datasets free (977 open datasets, 630 image and 110 video); listings show view and download counts but no buyer mix. Datasets such as K-Stock target gaps global stock sources leave.

Q2.answer: Providers opening data through AI-Hub are offered NIA-funded quality and de-identification support worth 60 million won per dataset, publicity and usage statistics; publication is decided by an NIA committee.

Q3.answer: Most inventory is built by vendor consortia under government programmes, with rights co-held by the builders and NIA; the rest comes from institutions, sovereign-model teams, companies and universities.

Q4.answer: Commercial resale of a dataset needs a separate agreement with the building organisation, which keeps co-ownership; NIA may change the terms without notice. No dispute over changed terms was found.

Q5.answer: NIA operates the platform with MSIT and co-holds rights with the builders; users bear all liability for misuse; providers bear liability for infringing content; AI-Hub warrants nothing about others' content.

Q6.answer: Open data is copied to the user's machine inside Korea; sensitive data (medical, broadcast) stays in the safe zone and only trained models leave; institution data and private exchanges are links.

Q7.answer: Listings assert that portrait and IP rights were cleared and data de-identified; a face dataset was cut back when consent forms were renewed; users must delete data containing personal information.

Q8.answer: A non-open licence by policy: for-profit R&D and selling trained models allowed, but no redistribution of raw data, no third-party sharing, attribution required, Korea-only use; NIA may demand destruction.

Q9.answer: No transaction: users apply with a purpose and identity check, most datasets are auto-approved for three months, and all access is free.

Q10.answer: A dataset is source data plus labelling data with train/validation/sample splits (test withheld), a version history and a three-month use approval; what happens to past downloads on revision is not stated.

Q11.answer: Before download users see full descriptions, schemas, statistics, a processed sample and baseline-vs-measured scores of a validation model; NIA publishes quality guidelines but disclaims others' content.

Q12.answer: AI-Hub is catalogue-only; for commercial and custom data it links out to four private exchanges including CrowdWorks's dataset store.

conflicts.resolution: The usage policy allows overseas entities to use the data under a separate agreement with the builders and NIA; the FAQ says data is hard to provide to anyone abroad or non-Korean regardless of affiliation. Both are live primary pages; the FAQ reads as current practice.

The data usage policy permits for-profit R&D, while the site-wide 2018 terms bar any profit-making use of the service without prior consent; the data-specific policy and FAQ (F5) appear to govern the data.
